papers.title: France’s south is testing out hard-right rule
papers.body_text: France’s south is testing out hard-right rule Europe | Provence of concept France’s south is testing out hard-right rule The National Rally is mixing raw nativism with promises of fiscal liberalism June 25th 2026 The BEACHfront in Nice is a spot for admiring the self as much as the sea. Biceps are big; dogs are tiny. Superyachts float in the bay. In short, not an obvious place to stir up populist indignation. Yet in March France’s fifth-biggest city was captured by a party allied to Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN), making it her biggest prize yet. Nice hints at how the nationalist right is conquering the south of France—and how it hopes, at the presidential election next April, to win the country. At this year’s local elections most big cities were won or held by the left or greens. Some in the south narrowly resisted the RN, including Marseille and Toulon. Nice was a crucial victory for the nationalist right because of both its size and location. The RN and its friends now run mid-sized town halls in a wide band of southern France that includes Beaucaire, Carpentras and Orange in Provence, Menton on the Riviera, and Carcassonne and Perpignan in the south-west. Eric Ciotti, the new mayor of Nice, who quit the centre-right Republicans to found his own party and hooked it up to the RN, promised to tighten security, cut waste and turn the page. The outgoing centrist mayor, Christian Estrosi, had held office for 17 years. Mr Ciotti’s tough law-and-order promises resonated. Away from the seafront cocktail bars, flanked by the airport and the motorway, lie the sprawling housing estates of the Moulins quarter. In May two bystanders were shot dead there by a man wielding an assault rifle. In the past two years drug-gang rivalry has led to 11 deaths. Mr Ciotti has opened a police outpost near the site of the shooting. He vows to increase by 50% the number of local police in the city by 2027. Yet the capture of Nice reveals something else: a potent new RN electoral strategy, embraced by Jordan Bardella, the party leader, which marries its traditional working-class base with a liberal-minded bourgeois electorate. This works in Nice and other southern towns with a history of leaning to the right, as well as a high share of pensioners, who tilt right too. Mr Ciotti cut the cordon sanitaire that previously made the RN untouchable. But he studiously balanced these links with the recruitment of moderate local notables. “We are the real party of the right,” he insists. It is a liberal fiscal message—“France wins the world cup for taxes,” he complains—with a populist twist. Mr Ciotti admits to admiring Argentina’s Javier Milei and his chainsaw, and has begun a showy assault on town-hall profligacy. In Nice families who display extravagant wealth coexist with others on squeezed budgets. Mr Ciotti has blended hardline anti-immigrant nativism with a clampdown on the town-hall car fleet and banquet budget. The politics play out differently across the south, where the RN has a long history. In the 1980s Jean-Marie Le Pen, Ms Le Pen’s father and the party’s co-founder, began to score in double digits in the region, drawing on xenophobia prompted in part by an influx of immigrant labour recruited from north Africa. In greater Nice 17% of the population are immigrants, compared to 12% in France as a whole. Identity politics is a common theme. Beaucaire is a Provençal town of shuttered façades dominated by a medieval fortress and a cement factory. Under RN rule for 12 years, the town hall flies only the French tricolore (not the European Union’s flag), and has revived folk traditions with an unapologetic Christian nod. Last year the town was fined €120,000 ($136,000) for refusing to dismantle a nativity scene, illegal in public buildings under France’s secular rules. This month Beaucaire organised a “weekend of tradition”, including a Provençal dance show, with free entry for all. Residents seem to appreciate hyper-localism: potted flowers, cleaner pavements, children’s summer activities. “Beaucaire has been transformed,” says a seller of tapenade at the weekday market. “It’s clean, there are no drug dealers, there are events for everyone.” Julien Sanchez, until recently its mayor, is now the RN’s campaign director. A study of RN governance by Fred Paxton and Timothy Peace, at the University of Glasgow, calls this approach “populist pragmatism”, part of a national strategy of mainstreaming the party. RN city governance has brought plenty of controversy. Several new RN mayors, including in Carcassonne, have stopped flying the EU flag. Many have cut subsidies to human-rights and immigrant-aid groups. Carcassonne has introduced a rule against begging. In Carpentras a song associated with the Nazi-collaborationist Vichy regime was broadcast through municipal loudspeakers on May 8th; its RN mayor denied responsibility. Nor are the RN and friends unstoppable in the south. Marseille was held by the left after the hard left stood down in the run-off against Ms Le Pen’s candidate; it showed the value of left-wing unity, which eludes national leaders. But the region now has a concentration of hard-right laboratories, which will test how competent—and how toxic—their leaders are. ■ To stay on top of the biggest European stories, sign up to Café Europa , our weekly subscriber-only newsletter. questions.stem: France’s south is testing out hard-right rule Europe | Provence of concept France’s south is testing out hard-right rule The National Rally is mixing raw nativism with promises of fiscal liberalism June 25th 2026 The BEACHfront in Nice is a spot for admiring the self as much as the sea. Biceps are big; dogs are tiny. Superyachts float in the bay. In short, not an obvious place to ____ populist indignation.
questions.explanation: 文章描述了在尼斯海滨这样一个看似平静的地方，却发生了政治上的转变。'Stir up' 在这里的意思是‘激起’，与‘populist indignation’（民粹主义愤慨）搭配，表示‘激起民粹主义愤慨’。选项 B 'elicit' (引起，激起) 最符合语境。A 'avert' (避免)，C 'suppress' (压制)，D 'quell' (镇压) 意思不符。

questions.stem: Yet in March France’s fifth-biggest city was ____ by a party allied to Marine Le Pen’s National Rally (RN), making it her biggest prize yet.
questions.explanation: 文章提到尼斯被国民联盟（RN）的盟友政党控制，这是一个重要的政治胜利。'Captured' (被占领，被攻占) 是原文的词，在这里表示‘被……夺取’。选项 B 'conquered' (被征服，被攻占) 最能表达这种政治上的胜利和控制。A 'reclaimed' (收复) 暗示之前是自己的，C 'ceded' (割让) 表示主动放弃，D 'negotiated' (谈判) 意思不符。

questions.stem: Nice hints at how the nationalist right is ____ the south of France—and how it hopes, at the presidential election next April, to win the country.
questions.explanation: 文章讨论了国民联盟如何在法国南部获得支持并扩大影响力。'Conquering' (征服) 是原文的词，此处指国民右翼正在逐步渗透并巩固其在法国南部的影响力。选项 A 'entrenching' (巩固，确立) 准确地描述了这种逐步深入并站稳脚跟的过程。B 'abandoning' (放弃) 意思相反，C 'challenging' (挑战) 程度不够，D 'penetrating' (渗透) 也有一定道理，但 'entrenching' 更强调其巩固地位的意味。

questions.stem: At this year’s local elections most big cities were won or held by the left or greens. Some in the south ____ resisted the RN, including Marseille and Toulon.
questions.explanation: 文章对比了不同城市在选举中的结果，指出一些南方城市‘勉强’抵抗了国民联盟。'Narrowly resisted' (勉强抵抗，以微弱优势抵抗) 是原文的表达。选项 A 'narrowly' (狭窄地，勉强地) 准确地传达了这个意思。B 'fiercely' (激烈地)，C 'initially' (起初)，D 'steadily' (稳步地) 都不符合原文的语境。

questions.stem: The RN and its friends now run mid-sized town halls in a wide band of southern France that includes Beaucaire, Carpentras and Orange in Provence, Menton on the Riviera, and Carcassonne and Perpignan in the ____.
questions.explanation: 文章列举了国民联盟在法国南部控制的城镇，并明确指出其中一些城镇的地理位置。原文 'south-west' (西南部) 指出了 Carcassonne 和 Perpignan 的具体方位。选项 C 'south-west' (西南部) 直接对应原文信息。

questions.stem: Eric Ciotti, the new mayor of Nice, who quit the centre-right Republicans to found his own party and ____ it up to the RN, promised to tighten security, cut waste and turn the page.
questions.explanation: 文章描述了埃里克·西奥蒂组建新党并与国民联盟建立联系的过程。'Hooked it up to' (将……连接到，与……挂钩) 是原文的表达，表示将自己的政党与国民联盟联系起来。选项 A 'hooked' (连接，挂钩) 是原文词，最贴切。B 'tied' (绑住)，C 'linked' (连接)，D 'wedded' (结合) 虽有相似之处，但 'hooked up' 表达了这种政治上的结盟关系。

questions.stem: Mr Ciotti’s tough law-and-order promises ____.
questions.explanation: 文章提到西奥蒂强硬的治安承诺引起了共鸣。'Resonated' (引起共鸣，反响强烈) 是原文的词，表示他的承诺受到了欢迎和响应。A 'resisted' (抵抗)，B 'receded' (后退)，D 'rebounded' (反弹) 意思不符。

questions.stem: Away from the seafront cocktail bars, flanked by the airport and the motorway, lie the sprawling housing ____ of the Moulins quarter.
questions.explanation: 文章描述了尼斯一个名为 Moulins 的区域，那里是住房区。'Housing estates' (住宅区，住房区) 是原文的表达，指大片成片的住宅。B 'complexes' (建筑群)，C 'districts' (区域)，D 'settlements' (住区，聚居地) 也可以表示居住区，但 'estates' 更常用于指规模较大的、规划过的住宅区域，符合原文的语境。

questions.stem: In May two bystanders were shot dead there by a man ____ an assault rifle.
questions.explanation: 文章描述了一起枪击事件，其中一名男子使用了攻击性步枪。'Wielding' (挥舞，使用) 是原文的词，强调的是‘使用’武器进行攻击。B 'carrying' (携带)，C 'holding' (拿着)，D 'brandishing' (挥舞，炫耀) 意思接近，但 'wielding' 更侧重于‘有效使用’武器进行攻击的行为。

questions.stem: Mr Ciotti has opened a police outpost near the site of the shooting. He ____ to increase by 50% the number of local police in the city by 2027.
questions.explanation: 文章提到西奥蒂承诺将增加警力。'Vows' (发誓，郑重承诺) 是原文的词，表示一种强烈的、郑重的承诺。B 'plans' (计划)，C 'aims' (旨在)，D 'intends' (打算) 程度和语气都比 'vows' 要弱。

questions.stem: Yet the capture of Nice reveals something else: a potent new RN electoral strategy, ____ by Jordan Bardella, the party leader, which marries its traditional working-class base with a liberal-minded bourgeois electorate.
questions.explanation: 文章描述了国民联盟新的选举策略，该策略被党领袖乔丹·巴尔德拉采纳。'Embraced' (拥抱，采纳) 是原文的词，表示‘采纳’或‘接受’这个策略。B 'proposed' (提议)，C 'initiated' (发起)，D 'championed' (倡导) 也有‘推行’的意味，但 'embraced' 更贴切地表达了党领袖接受并推行这一策略。

questions.stem: This works in Nice and other southern towns with a history of leaning to the right, as well as a high share of pensioners, who tilt right ____.
questions.explanation: 文章指出，尼斯和其他一些南部城镇的选民结构（包括高比例的退休人员）有利于国民联盟的策略。'Too' (也) 在这里表示‘同样地’，与前面的‘lean to the right’相呼应，表示退休人员‘也’倾向于右翼。B 'also' (也) 也可以，但 'too' 在句末更自然。C 'either' (要么) 意思不符。D 'likewise' (同样地) 也可以，但 'too' 在此更常用。

questions.stem: Mr Ciotti cut the cordon ____ that previously made the RN untouchable. But he studiously balanced these links with the recruitment of moderate local notables.
questions.explanation: 文章提到西奥蒂打破了之前使国民联盟‘不可接触’的‘隔离带’。'Cordon sanitaire' (隔离带，封锁线) 是一个固定短语，特指为了阻止某种政治势力（尤其是极端主义）蔓延而建立的政治或社会屏障。选项 A 'sanitaire' (卫生，健康的，象征性的‘隔离’) 是构成此短语的词，最符合语境。

questions.stem: It is a liberal fiscal message— “France wins the world cup for taxes,” he complains—with a populist ____.
questions.explanation: 文章描述了西奥蒂的政治信息，既有自由主义的财政主张，又有民粹主义的‘特色’或‘转折’。'Populist twist' (民粹主义的转折/变味) 是原文的表达，表示在自由主义信息中加入民粹主义的元素，使其更具吸引力。B 'edge' (优势，锋芒)，C 'tone' (语调)，D 'flavor' (风味) 意思略有偏差，'twist' 更强调在原有信息上的‘扭转’或‘改变’。

questions.stem: Mr Ciotti admits to admiring Argentina’s Javier Milei and his chainsaw, and has begun a showy assault on town-hall ____.
questions.explanation: 文章提到西奥蒂模仿哈维尔·米莱，开始攻击市政厅的‘铺张浪费’。'Profligacy' (挥霍，浪费，恣睢) 是原文的词，指不必要的、过度的开支。B 'inefficiency' (低效)，C 'corruption' (腐败)，D 'extravagance' (奢侈，铺张) 意思相近，但 'profligacy' 最贴切地描述了市政厅在支出上的‘浪费’和‘铺张’。

questions.stem: In Nice families who display extravagant wealth coexist with others on squeezed ____.
questions.explanation: 文章描绘了尼斯社会阶层的差异，富裕家庭与‘预算紧张’的家庭并存。'Squeezed budgets' (预算紧张) 是原文的表达，指收入有限，开支受到严格限制。B 'incomes' (收入)，C 'finances' (财务状况)，D 'resources' (资源) 都可以与‘squeezed’搭配，但 'budgets' 最直接地表达了‘可支配资金’的紧张。

questions.stem: Mr Ciotti has blended hardline anti-immigrant nativism with a clampdown on the town-hall car fleet and ____ budget.
questions.explanation: 文章提到西奥蒂一方面采取强硬的反移民政策，另一方面又着手削减市政厅的开支，包括公务用车和‘宴会’预算。'Banquet budget' (宴会预算) 是原文的表达，指用于举办宴会的开销。B 'entertainment' (娱乐)，C 'travel' (差旅)，D 'office' (办公) 都有可能被削减，但 'banquet' 是原文明确提到的。

questions.stem: In the 1980s Jean-Marie Le Pen, Ms Le Pen’s father and the party’s co-founder, began to score in double digits in the region, drawing on xenophobia ____ in part by an influx of immigrant labour recruited from north Africa.
questions.explanation: 文章解释了让-马里·勒庞在80年代获得支持的原因，包括利用了因北非移民涌入而产生的‘仇外心理’。'Prompted in part by' (部分由……引起/促成) 是原文的表达，表示移民涌入是导致仇外心理产生的部分原因。B 'caused' (导致)，C 'inspired' (激励)，D 'triggered' (触发) 都有‘引起’的意思，但 'prompted' 更侧重于‘促使’或‘刺激’，并且常与‘in part’搭配，表示部分原因。

questions.stem: Last year the town was fined €120,000 ($136,000) for refusing to dismantle a nativity scene, illegal in public buildings under France’s ____ rules.
questions.explanation: 文章提到博凯尔因拒绝拆除公共建筑中的耶稣诞生场景而被罚款，这违反了法国的‘政教分离’原则。'Secular' (世俗的，政教分离的) 是原文的词，指法国法律不允许在公共场所进行宗教展示。B 'religious' (宗教的) 意思相反，C 'national' (国家的)，D 'traditional' (传统的) 均不符合语境。

questions.stem: A study of RN governance by Fred Paxton and Timothy Peace, at the University of Glasgow, calls this approach “populist ____”, part of a national strategy of mainstreaming the party.
questions.explanation: 文章引用一项研究，将国民联盟的治理方式称为‘民粹实用主义’。'Populist pragmatism' (民粹实用主义) 是原文的表达，指在实践中采取民粹主义策略，注重实际效果。B 'idealism' (理想主义)，C 'realism' (现实主义)，D 'nationalism' (民族主义) 虽有相关性，但 'pragmatism' 最准确地概括了‘populist pragmatism’这个术语。

papers.title: Was it a mistake for 99 Colombian guerrillas to lay down their arms?
papers.body_text: In mid-June, 99 guerrilla fighters were flown by helicopter to a small settlement in a rural area of southern Colombia where they lined up and, one by one, handed their weapons to government officials: rifles, pistols, machine guns and grenade launchers. They also stripped off their heavy tactical vests, field packs and camouflage uniforms, which were each piled into a bonfire to mark the beginning of a new life away from an armed conflict that has claimed nearly half a million lives in the last six decades. That was precisely what the former president Gustavo Petro’s “total peace” plan had sought to achieve: negotiating with and disarming all of Colombia’s criminal groups, which are estimated to have nearly 30,000 members. But the group of just 99 people was the only one to disarm, and did so just three days before the presidential runoff, which was won by the far-right millionaire lawyer Abelardo de la Espriella, who had campaigned on a promise to end “total peace” and return to a full-on strategy of jailing or killing criminals. Now, several weeks after the new president took office – and amid efforts to deal with the aftermath of the 7.4-magnitude earthquake, as his government has already begun the promised airstrikes against criminal groups – the 99 do not know what will happen to them. “We’re in limbo,” said Natalia Bríñez, 29, one of 13 women among the group staying in the temporary location zone, or ZUT by its Spanish initials, a government-controlled zone where, under surveillance and unable to leave, they were supposed to make the transition to civilian life over the following months. View image in fullscreen Natalia Briñez, a former guerrilla fighter, is one of 13 women in the ZUT. Photograph: Daniela Díaz/The Guardian The former guerrillas are housed in beige brick buildings decorated with drawings they painted themselves, including doves of peace, with a communal dining hall where three meals a day are served. No weapons are allowed inside and soldiers guard the ZUT from a perimeter less than a mile away. One former combatant built a makeshift gym with weights made from metal pipes and tins filled with cement and sand, and there is an improvised football pitch, but most of them spend their days on their phones. De la Espriella has repeatedly said his government will no longer negotiate peace agreements and has yet to announce what he intends to do regarding the people at the ZUT. The president has not responded to requests for comment. In theory, any arrest warrants against the group are suspended, and they remain under state protection until 25 December, when Petro’s decree establishing the ZUT expires. But De la Espriella could revoke the decree at any time. Armando Novoa, the former government official who led peace negotiations with the group, said “the worst-case scenario would be for the new government to close the ZUT, launch a military operation and try to capture or kill them. That would be a crime against humanity, because these people are unarmed.” Between 2 and 4 August, days before De la Espriella’s inauguration, Novoa led journalists including the Guardian through the ZUT. The Office of the High Commissioner for Peace, where he worked, has since been absorbed into the newly created National Security Commission – a move expected to result in more than 200 job losses – and Novoa has resigned. For now, at least, the ZUT remains in operation and has a small library run by Bríñez, who has a phoenix tattoo on her left shoulder as a symbol of her rebirth away from the armed conflict. View image in fullscreen No weapons are allowed inside the ZUT and soldiers guard it from a perimeter less than a mile away. Photograph: Daniela Díaz/The Guardian “The hardest thing for me has been being away from my children,” said Bríñez, who has a seven-year-old daughter and a 10-year-old son and speaks to them on video calls, but will only be able to see them in person once her “transition” is complete, a process that includes vocational training and psychosocial support. They were also supposed to receive financial support of about £425 a month, which had not yet been paid. In the meantime, some of them were planning to start a chicken-rearing business. The 99 made up a small part of a group of about 1,000 combatants called Commandos of the Frontier – most of whom remain armed – and are part of the National Coordinator of the Bolivarian Army (CNEB), a former dissident faction of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc) with about 2,500 members which controls the border with Ecuador. The Petro administration said negotiations were also under way with other members of the CNEB, who published an open letter addressed to De la Espriella saying they were willing to continue talks with him. It is not known whether the president responded. View image in fullscreen One of the works of graffiti in the ZUT painted by the former guerrillas. Photograph: Daniela Díaz/The Guardian The CNEB’s chief “peace negotiator”, Geovany Andrés Rojas, known as “Araña” (Spider), had been in custody since February under a US extradition request for drug trafficking, which Petro had delayed. Last Wednesday, De la Espriella ordered extradition. Although such groups emerged in the 1960s as leftwing rebels fighting government abuses and seeking revolution – followed soon afterwards by far-right paramilitary groups – ideology has long since been overtaken for most of them by economic interests, above all drug trafficking (Colombia is the world’s largest producer of cocaine) and illegal mining. “Here in the ZUT, the vast majority were not in the group because of any ideological commitment, but for economic reasons,” said Novoa. “It even surprised us that most of them simply called the group ‘the company’.” Petro repeatedly tried to negotiate peace agreements with larger groups. The armed factions took advantage of temporary ceasefires to continue expanding, a process that had already begun before he took office. They also clashed among themselves for control of territory and illicit economies, which many security experts say contributed to a rise in homicides, kidnappings and massacres. “Total peace” was an attempt to address what the landmark 2016 peace deal between the government and the Farc failed to resolve, as other armed groups and Farc dissidents remained active. Petro’s administration failed to reduce violence, which instead reached its worst levels in a decade, and to reach the disarmament stage with any of the gangs, apart from the 99 former combatants – who handed over their weapons only on the eve of an election that every poll indicated the government-backed candidate would lose. “They [the government] told us: ‘If this works, you’re opening the door for other groups and will set an example,’” said Bríñez. Some security experts saw the agreement as rushed. View image in fullscreen Former guerrillas in the ZUT have little to do and spend much of their time looking at their phones. Photograph: Daniela Díaz/The Guardian “It was a somewhat irresponsible decision,” said Paula Tobo, a senior researcher at the thinktank Ideas for Peace Foundation, which published an extensive report on why Total Peace failed. Tobo said the 99 were now in a “legal limbo” because their protection rested on decrees that could be revoked and there is no legal framework for their transition to civilian life. All of the Petro administration’s proposals to regulate surrenders failed in Congress and, under current law, anyone who has committed crimes such as kidnapping or drug trafficking is not eligible for amnesty. “It’s positive that these people wanted to lay down their arms, but it really wasn’t the right time for the government to take that decision … The previous administration clearly put them at risk of this government suddenly deciding to abolish the ZUT and arrest them,” said Tobo. View image in fullscreen A wristband with the logo of the armed group to which Adrián, 19, belonged. Photograph: Daniela Díaz/The Guardian The group wrote a letter to De la Espriella reaffirming its “irreversible decision to commit to peace” and inviting him to visit the ZUT. At the time of publication it had received no response. The youngest member of the group, a 19-year-old who asked to be identified only as Adrián, said they wanted “to have a home, a family”. However, he knows what he will do if things do not go according to plan. “Honestly, I’d take up arms again, because we’re keeping our side of the bargain and the government should do the same, shouldn’t it?” he said. Daniela Díaz travelled to Valle del Guamuez at the invitation of the Colombian government’s former Office of the High Commissioner for Peace.

questions.stem: The article describes the disarmament of 99 guerrilla fighters in Colombia. What was the primary purpose of the 'total peace' plan mentioned in the text?

options.A: To negotiate with and disarm all of Colombia's criminal groups.
options.B: To exclusively focus on arresting and jailing criminals.
options.C: To initiate airstrikes against all armed factions.
options.D: To provide immediate financial support and housing to all former combatants.

questions.explanation: 文章开头明确指出，前总统 Gustavo Petro 的“总和平”计划旨在“与哥伦比亚所有犯罪集团进行谈判并解除他们的武装”。选项 B 和 C 描述了新总统 de la Espriella 的策略，而非 Petro 的“总和平”计划。选项 D 提到了计划的一部分内容，但并非计划的主要目的。

questions.stem: Why did the group of 99 former guerrilla fighters find themselves in a state of 'limbo' after disarming?

options.A: They were awaiting the results of an election that would determine their future.
options.B: The new president, Abelardo de la Espriella, had promised to revoke the 'total peace' plan and take immediate action.
options.C: The temporary location zone (ZUT) they were housed in was scheduled to close immediately after their disarmament.
options.D: They had not yet received the promised financial support and vocational training.

questions.explanation: 文章提到，在新总统 de la Espriella 上任后，尽管 99 名战士已解除武装并被安置在 ZUT，但新总统承诺结束“总和平”计划，并已开始对犯罪集团进行空袭。这使得这 99 人对自己的未来感到不确定，即处于“limbo”状态。选项 A 提及了选举，但并非他们处于 limbo 的直接原因。选项 C 不准确，ZUT 的关闭并非立即发生。选项 D 提到了他们未收到的支持，但这更多是 limbo 状态下的一种具体困境，而非 limbo 状态形成的主要原因。

questions.stem: What is the main reason cited in the article for the shift in ideology within Colombian armed groups since the 1960s?

options.A: A stronger commitment to leftwing revolutionary ideals.
options.C: The dominance of economic interests, particularly drug trafficking, over political ideology.
options.D: The successful implementation of previous peace agreements with Farc.

questions.explanation: 文章指出，尽管这些团体最初是作为左翼反叛分子出现的，但“意识形态早已被经济利益所取代，尤其是毒品贩运（哥伦比亚是世界上最大的可卡因生产国）和非法采矿。” 这直接表明经济利益已成为主导因素。选项 A 与文章内容相反。选项 B 文章未提及。选项 D 文章指出 2016 年的和平协议未能解决所有问题，暗示了其局限性，而非成功实施导致了意识形态转变。

questions.stem: According to Paula Tobo, a senior researcher at the Ideas for Peace Foundation, what is the primary issue with the current situation of the 99 former guerrillas?

options.A: They are not receiving adequate vocational training for civilian life.
options.B: Their legal protection is based on decrees that can be easily revoked, and there is no established legal framework for their transition.
options.C: The new government has failed to respond to their request for amnesty.
options.D: They are at high risk of being re-recruited by other armed groups due to lack of support.

questions.explanation: Paula Tobo 明确表示，这 99 人处于“法律上的灰色地带”（legal limbo），因为他们的保护依赖于可以撤销的法令，并且“没有他们向平民生活过渡的法律框架”。选项 A 是他们面临的困境之一，但不是 Tobo 指出的主要问题。选项 C 文章提到他们的情况，但 Tobo 的评论侧重于法律框架的缺失。选项 D 是潜在风险，但 Tobo 的直接论点是法律和保护的不确定性。

questions.stem: What does the statement 'We’re in limbo' by Natalia Bríñez suggest about the former guerrillas' current situation?

options.A: They are actively engaged in new civilian jobs and reintegration programs.
options.B: They are uncertain about their future due to the change in government and policy.
options.C: They are satisfied with the temporary housing and support provided by the government.
options.D: They are planning to resume their armed activities due to lack of governmental support.

questions.explanation: “Limbo”一词通常表示一种不确定、悬而未决的状态。在文章的语境下，99 名前游击队员在解除武装后，新政府上台并改变了政策，使得他们对未来的待遇和安排感到迷茫和不确定。选项 A 与文章描述的“spend much of their time looking at their phones”和等待支持的情况不符。选项 C 与文章中描述的未收到款项和对未来的担忧相悖。选项 D 是该前战斗人员 Adrián 提到的一个备用计划，但 Bríñez 的“limbo”表述更多是指当前的不确定状态，而非立即的行动计划。

papers.title: Young Chinese-Irish ballroom dancer goes international
papers.body_text: Kerry Sui and Francis Carty perform on the dance floor at Blackpool Dance Festival in November. [Photo provided to chinadaily.com.cn] Kerry Sui, a 10-year-old Chinese-Irish dancer, and her dance partner Francis Carty are set to compete in Italy and perform on Chinese TV after winning the British juvenile ballroom championship. Kerry and Francis, who is also 10, won the British National Juvenile Ballroom trophy and took first prize last month in the juvenile Latin category at the Blackpool Dance Festival. Kerry was born in Dublin and lives there with her parents, who emigrated from China. Her Chinese name is Sui Yuanjing. She started ballroom and Latin dancing four years ago and was partnered earlier this year with Francis, who lives in the English county of Shropshire. The two were friends before they performed together and Kerry said their friendship is one of the best things about her dancing partnership with Francis. Their hard work, under the guidance of teachers Laura O'Brien and David and Helen Truman, meant Kerry and Francis have seen quite a lot of success. "When Francis is stressed, I can calm him down, because he hasn't really been in many big competitions, such as the nationals and internationals," Kerry said. "My mum said I have to guide him." Francis said Kerry has a positive attitude and described her as always remaining upbeat. And they both have a dance that they like the least: the tango. "The tango is like an angry dance, you have to be sharp," Kerry said. The dancers often visit each other's families and describe their friendship and their teachers' involvement as like being in a big family. She said a visit to China put a strain on the close bonds. "I was in China for six weeks and there was a dance studio there where I would practice, but I felt lonely," Kerry said. Francis described the time they spent apart as "horrible". Kerry and Francis were training on Saturday in Wolverhampton, a city in England's West Midlands region, in advance of a competition in Stoke-on-Trent on Sunday. The event was cancelled due to the heavy snowfall across parts of the United Kingdom. The pair head to Italy in January for a competition, before jetting off to China to appear on a TV show.

questions.stem: What is the primary significance of the British National Juvenile Ballroom trophy for Kerry Sui and Francis Carty?

options.A: It marks the formal beginning of their dance partnership.
options.B: It qualifies them for upcoming international performances and competitions.
options.C: It is the only award they have received since they began dancing.
options.D: It highlights their expertise in the tango, their favorite dance style.

questions.explanation: 文章提到Kerry和Francis赢得英国青少年标准舞锦标赛冠军后，即将在意大利参赛并在中国电视节目中表演，因此该奖项是他们走向国际舞台的跳板。选项A与文中所述“今年早些时候搭档”不符，C项错误，D项与文中提到他们最不喜欢探戈矛盾。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what role does Kerry play in her partnership with Francis?

options.A: She acts as a mentor who teaches him the fundamentals of Latin dance.
options.B: She serves as a supportive influence to help him manage competition pressure.
options.C: She is responsible for organizing their travel arrangements to Italy and China.
options.D: She feels that her experience in China makes her the superior dancer.

questions.explanation: 文中Kerry提到Francis在面对大赛时会感到压力，而她能够让他平静下来，因为她的母亲叮嘱她要引导他。这证明了她在搭档中起到了心理支持和引导的作用。

questions.stem: How did Kerry and Francis feel about their separation during the visit to China?

options.A: It allowed them to focus on individual training without distraction.
options.B: It strengthened their discipline through independent practice.
options.C: It was described as a negative and isolating experience for both.
options.D: It caused a permanent rift in their professional partnership.

questions.explanation: 文中明确提到Kerry在练习时感到孤独（lonely），而Francis将他们分开的时间描述为“糟糕的”（horrible），可见分离对他们两人都是负面体验。

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the dancers' view on the tango?

options.A: They believe it requires an aggressive personality to perform effectively.
options.B: They find it technically easier to master compared to other dances.
options.C: They dislike it because they struggle with its sharp, intense movements.
options.D: They consider it a joyful dance that celebrates their friendship.

questions.explanation: 文中指出他们最不喜欢探戈，并提到探戈像是一种“愤怒的舞蹈”，要求动作“尖锐（sharp）”。这暗示了他们对这种舞蹈风格的排斥感，认为它不符合他们的舞蹈偏好。

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the nature of the partnership between Kerry and Francis?

options.A: A strictly professional relationship focused solely on training.
options.B: A familial bond characterized by mutual support and friendship.
options.C: A distant collaboration complicated by geographic and cultural differences.
options.D: An inconsistent partnership prone to frequent conflict due to high pressure.

questions.explanation: 文中多次提到他们是好朋友，且将他们与家人及老师的关系形容为“大家庭”，并强调了他们互相支持的友情，说明这不仅是专业上的合作，更是深厚的情感联结。

papers.title: Chapter 14
papers.body_text: | Next | Section menu | Main menu | Previous | Alana Hope Levinson Culture Apr 1, 2026 6:00 AM Taylor Lorenz’s Screen Time Is Almost 17 Hours a Day. 17!!! The extremely online journalist and content creator doesn’t believe in tech hygiene and yearns for a world where “inbox infinity” is celebrated. Illustration: Òscar Climent Ollet; Getty Images Taylor Lorenz doesn’t want to touch grass. The technology and culture journalist wrote the bestselling book Extremely Online : The Untold Story of Fame, Influence, and Power on the Internet, and she has the screen time to prove it. Previously a reporter for mainstream media outlets, Lorenz built such a rabid following (and a legion of haters) that she decided to go independent in 2024. Now, almost 100,000 fans subscribe to her newsletter, User Mag , for her insider knowledge of virality and her freakish ability to contextualize how internet culture shapes, well, everything. For our very first User Behavior , Lorenz defends her extreme digital diet, revealing how she’s first to the AI slop, what it takes to run a meme page , and why she’s not worried about any of this rotting her brain. A regular series that quantifies the tech lifestyles of the rich and/or famous. Phone model: iPhone 15 Pro I’m waiting for a decent upgrade. I'll upgrade when I get a better camera. I'm friends with an influencer marketing person at Apple, and I've never gotten a single free product out of it. It's a disappointment. I'm not big-time enough to make it on the gifting! Computer model: 2024 MacBook Pro, 14-Inch Standard. Good computer. When I was quitting my job, I thought, what's the closest to my work computer? And I bought that. Also, I edit video. So I need a little more horsepower. My iPhone screen time is around 10 hours or something. I am sort of horrified, but the thing is, for some reason, writing is less stressful to me on my phone. So I often write the first draft of everything on my phone. I am using it for work; I'm not just on brain-rot Instagram Reels. I also like to listen to background noise all day, because I hate the silence of downtown LA. I just always have music on. And so my two most used apps are Spotify and YouTube. At night, I like to watch Netflix on my phone because I'm still on my family plan and I can only add so many devices. I think caring about screen time is stupid. It's a waste of mental energy. I actually think this whole moral panic over screen time is going to be gone in 10 years, because everything's going to be integrated into the world around us already. If you're talking to an AI agent all day and just telling it what to do and interacting with it, you're not going to have to look at a screen. You'll probably just be speaking to some pod in your ear. Music app: Spotify, Hype Machine I think I’m one of the last remaining users of Hype Machine, which was really popular during the bloghouse era. It started in 2005 as a way to discover MP3 blogs. I think I started using it in 2010, and I feel like I discover lots of new music on there and also they have remixes and stuff. It's honestly the best, and everybody needs to support them. I'm constantly concerned about them going out of business, because they're just from the indie internet a long time ago. I don't like the AI playlist and the AI-ification of music recommendations. I like to be given music that I would've never found before. I like the discovery aspect of Hype Machine, because it's curated by bloggers, and there are still music bloggers out there, and they're finding stuff that I wouldn't have found otherwise. I listen to podcasts 24/7 on Spotify, and I do listen to music on Spotify. I just don't discover new music there as much. I do subscribe to today's top hits. I like pop music. Number of unread emails: 15,607 I don't believe in Inbox Zero. You kind of just have to treat email as a newsfeed or a Twitter feed—you're going to miss some stuff, but you can't worry about it. You just have to let it go and check in on it sometimes. A lot of people's stress about technology is feeling like they have to complete things or optimize, and I'm just like, whatever. If I see it, I see it. If it's really urgent, someone will find a way to reach me. Number of unread texts: 712 This number is very down. I was in the thousands. Because I'm in a lot of group chats, if I don't mark the group chats as read, it just becomes a really big number. But I've been moving a lot of my messages to Signal. I don't have any anxiety about any of it. Who cares? There's this whole industry built on making you check your phone and making you feel like you have to check your phone. And again, I mean, this has gotten me in trouble at work before. It's not a great attitude to have in a job situation, but now that I'm self-employed, I don't have a boss telling me to check my email. It's the only way to live. I couldn't get my work done if I was checking texts and email and stuff. It's too much. Why are we in this cult? Last person FaceTimed: Barrie Segal (friend) I don't do a lot of FaceTime. Some friends FaceTime me, but I'm not an outgoing FaceTime person. I mostly FaceTime to gossip. It's great for gossiping, because it's like you're there with them. Gossip is kind of intimate. You've got to FaceTime to make sure that no one's around. Because if you just call and start gossiping, that's a very risky endeavor. Last thing Googled: “WSJ A-hed” This is so embarrassing. I Google that every day. I don't even know what that is, but it's the only thing I read in The Wall Street Journal. I don't know why it's called A-hed. They're all just entertaining stories. Last photo taken : A girl at an anti-ICE protest dragging an ICE agent piñata Courtesy of Taylor Lorenz Last AI prompt: “Vegan chickpea recipe garlic eggplant tahini” My AI history is all just random food assortments. I know AI is bad, blah, blah, blah, but I use it for recipes all the time. I usually use Gemini. Top three emoji: 💓 🫠 🙌 The heart is always my number one emoji. And then the other two I just kind of cycle through based on whatever I was texting. I use 🫠 a lot as a reaction to things like “LOL.” It’s also like, the world is bleak. I think I was using it in relation to Jasmine Crockett's Super Bowl ad today. Favorite social network: X Ugh, I’m a sicko. X is a terrible right-wing propaganda platform that Elon Musk has bastardized. I know it's a very skewed information environment. It incentivizes toxic behavior. But I love real-time information, and there just is no other platform that provides real-time information at scale that can also give you such a wide-ranging view into different communities. I'm very into tech Twitter, but I hate them all, and I want to see what everyone's up to. I want to see the latest discourse about Alex Karp's latest interview or something. If you want to follow what's going on in Silicon Valley, you’ve got to be on X. Least favorite social network: Threads Max Read coined calling Threads the “ gas-leak social network ,” and it is the perfect description. Threads is absolutely a bizarro world of some of the least media-literate people I've ever encountered. It's crazy. It's like a mix of brand content, hardcore blue MAGA, sort of liberal conspiracism, just really wild AI-generated headlines. There's so much fighting on Threads. It’s truly just a giant soup of misinformation and delusion. Favorite news source: Terrence O’Connor’s weekly cultural digest videos on TikTok I like the presentation. It’s a lot of news that I'm going to probably see on PopCrave, but he adds his own analysis. He is extremely good at recognizing things that are in the zeitgeist. Favorite subreddit: r/SubredditDrama I love to know the drama. I think mod drama is an eternal form of content on the internet, and I love to keep tabs on what's going on. I also think this subreddit provides a good picture of the social dynamics that are happening on Reddit broadly. Favorite tech product: 15-foot iPhone charging cord I have these cords everywhere. Any room that I'm in, I bring it. I don't like to feel tethered. It's so humiliating to have to sit next to an outlet and charge your phone. Number of burner accounts: unknown I just make them all the time. The only way to understand a community or trend or phenomenon, you have to get into that world. I also love Real Housewives and Bravo. And so I have a lot of accounts that just exist to follow Summer House news or Bravo, whatever. Because we don't have any sort of coherent tech policy that would give us the ability to exert control over our feeds, I feel like I just have to constantly make new burner feeds to get the information that I want and break out of what my personal algorithm would show me. Nostalgic tech obsession: Tumblr, BlackBerry Pearl I remember I had a rule: I would never date anyone that doesn't have BBM, because how am I going to communicate with them? BBM is life. And me and my best friend had both got Blackberry Pearls at the same time, and it was everything to me. I remember getting convinced to get an iPhone finally, and I was like, “God, I'm going to have to give up BBM.” And then I got the iPhone and totally never looked back. But I also loved the keyboard of it all. I had many Tumblrs. This is how I got into media. I was really big on the single-serving Tumblrs. There was a whole trend: "Fuck yeah, bagels.” “Fuck yeah, L Train.” Or whatever. Most of my Tumblrs were submission-based, but I just loved the discovery aspect. I deleted a lot of them, because I don't know what I was reblogging in 2011. I don't think it was problematic. It was just a weird era of internet content. I do still have “Fuck yeah, communism.” “Tech hygiene” ranking, out of 10: 7 I don't buy into any of the classic “tech hygiene” stuff. Maybe I'm just a pig or something, but the movement exists to cause people stress and anxiety. And I think you just have to relax a little bit and not think about it. But I do try to be good about privacy. I don't post certain things, but overall, just have a secure password. Everything else, don't stress about it. Everyone has our data anyway. Last screenshot: Clavicular I have a meme page, Taylor Lorenz 3.0 , so my screenshots are just content that I'm going to post. I would say I take probably dozens, if not hundreds, of screenshots a day. My default bookmarking is screenshotting and faving. Last internet rabbit hole: Melania movie meme conspiracy A few days ago I noticed that dozens (I think actually hundreds) of meme pages were all posting the exact same memes about the Melania movie . They were appearing on everything from many many cat-theme pages , to a page dedicated to Twin Towers remembrance , a Millie Bobby Brown stan account , to pages about boxing , astronomy , and scuba diving adventures . None of the posts had any ad disclosure. Also, the posts are getting terrible engagement, but the meme pages are keeping them
